mainEntity.name: What does Stellar Property Management do?

acceptedAnswer.text: We are a Chicago community association management firm. We manage condominium, HOA and townhome associations only.
Yes. We hold Illinois Community Association Management Firm license 291000211.

mainEntity.name: How long has Stellar been in business?
How many associations do you manage?

acceptedAnswer.text: We charge a customized flat fee starting at $20 per unit per month, with no separate capital-project oversight fee.
Chicago neighborhoods from Rogers Park to Hyde Park, plus the North Shore. See stellarpropertygroup.com/service-areas.

mainEntity.name: Who makes repair and funding decisions?

acceptedAnswer.text: The association's board of directors. As managing agent, we coordinate vendors and repairs and keep owners informed.

mainEntity.name: Are you the same as Stellar Properties Inc. or Stellar Management NY?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. We are a separate Chicago firm at 5107 N Western Ave.

mainEntity.name: How is Stellar different from large national management firms?

acceptedAnswer.text: Every community receives a dedicated property manager, transparent flat-fee pricing instead of percentage-based fees, and a local Chicago office that answers 24/7. National firms manage by volume; we manage by standard — which is why we maintain a 96% client retention rate since 2007, today across 29 associations.

mainEntity.name: How do we switch from our current management company to Stellar?

acceptedAnswer.text: Switching is a managed 30–60 day transition. Once your board signs, we handle everything: records retrieval from the outgoing firm, banking migration, vendor transfers, owner communication, and portal setup. Most boards describe the change as far easier than they expected.

Yes. A live member of our Chicago team answers our emergency line around the clock — never an outsourced call center. Vetted crews are dispatched immediately for floods, boiler failures, elevator entrapment, and other urgent events, with a full incident report delivered to your board.

mainEntity.name: Does Stellar offer resources for condo owners and residents, not just boards?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Beyond the resident portal, we publish The Owner’s Companion at stellarpropertygroup.com/condo-living — a free eight-chapter guide to living well in a condo or HOA, covering what assessments pay for, who fixes what, HO-6 insurance, owner rights under Illinois law, and what to do when something goes wrong.

mainEntity.name: What should a Chicago condo or HOA board look for when hiring a management company?

acceptedAnswer.text: Check five things: an active Illinois Community Association Management Firm license, a credentialed manager (CMCA, AMS or PCAM), a flat fee in writing instead of a percentage of the budget, a local office and a person who answers emergencies 24/7, and a written 30–60 day transition plan. Stellar Property Management meets all five — firm license #291000211, a CMCA- and AMS-credentialed principal, pricing from $20 per unit per month, an office at 5107 N Western Ave, Chicago — and offers a free scorecard for comparing proposals at stellarpropertygroup.com/tools/compare-management-proposals.

mainEntity.name: Is Stellar Property Management the same company as Stellar Property Group?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Stellar Property Group Inc. is the legal name of the Illinois corporation, which operates as Stellar Property Management — the same Chicago condo, HOA and townhome management firm at 5107 N Western Ave #1S, phone 773-728-0652. It is not related to other businesses that use the name Stellar, such as Stellar Properties Inc. of Carol Stream or Stellar Management of New York.

The Proposal
A private walk-through of your property, a review of financials and governing documents, and a bespoke management scope — never a one-size-fits-all package.

A managed 30–60 day handover. We retrieve records, migrate banking and vendor relationships, and brief every stakeholder — your board lifts a finger only to sign.
The Standard
Your dedicated manager is live, portals are open, and the first monthly report arrives on schedule. From here, the standard only rises.
